evidence: Cic. ND 2.138: sanguis per vēnās in omne corpus diffunditur et spīritus per artēriās
terms.comment: Ancient anatomy held that the arteries carried air (spīritus, Cic. ND 2.138). The word’s older sense is the windpipe (see windpipe), which the physicians called aspera artēria.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 57, 273.
